Clca 13 to 21 inches, light brownish gray (2.5Y 6/2) heavy silty clay loam, olive brown (2.5Y 4/3) moist; weak medium prismatic structure parting to weak, medium blocks; very hard, firm, sticky and plastic; strongly effervescent; common, medium and coarse masses of lime; gradual wavy boundary.
C2ca 21 to 26 inches, light brownish gray (2.5Y 6/2) silty clay, dark grayish brown (2.5Y 4/2) moist; moderate, medium subangular blocky structure; very hard, very firm, very sticky and plastic; strongly effervescent; common coarse masses of lime; gradual wavy boundary.
26 to 33 inches, pale olive (5Y 6/3) clay, olive (5Y 4/3) moist; massive, very hard, very firm, very sticky and very plastic; strongly effervescent; common very coarse masses of lime; common weathered shale chips; gradual wavy boundary.
IIC 33 to 41 inches, thin platy clay shale.
Depth to calcareous material ranges from 9 to 15 inches. The depth to bedrock ranges from 20 to 40 inches. The soil color hue in the Al and B2t horizons is 2.5Y and 10YR. Color range is light brownish gray, grayish brown, brown and light olive brown. The Cca horizon has hue of 2.5Y and 5Y. Color range is light brownish gray, pale olive, and light yellowish brown. Segregated lime is in few to common, medium and coarse soft masses.
Renohill soils are associated with Midway, Thurlow and Hydro soils. They are deeper to shale than the Midway soils. They have shale bedrock at shallower depths than the Thurlow and Hydro soils. The combined thickness of their A and B horizons is less than the Hydro soils.
Renohill silty clay loam, undulating (4 to 8 percent slopes) (Re).
This soil is on broad ridge tops and tablelands crossed by shallow drainageways. The soil has the profile described as typical for the series. The areas range in size from 20 to 50 acres. Included with this soil in mapping are areas of Midway silty clay loam on narrow ridges and Thurlow silty clay loam and Heldt silty clay loam in concave heads of drainageways. A few surface pebbles occur where terraces once covered the shaleland.
The surface runoff is medium, and the erosion hazard is moderate.
This soil is suited to dryland crops and range.
(Capatility Unit IIIe-3 Dryland; Clayey range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 2M).
